law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
title: Clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms before obtaining billing information
summary: Before collecting the consumer's billing information, the seller must provide text that clearly and conspicuously discloses all material terms of the transaction: that the consumer will be charged on a recurring basis until they cancel, the amount and frequency of the charges, any free-trial length and the charge after it, and how to cancel.
remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
title: Obtain express informed consent before charging
summary: The seller must obtain the consumer's express informed consent before charging the consumer's credit card, debit card, bank account or other financial account for the negative-option product or service.
remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)

remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

law: Electronic Fund Transfer Act / Regulation E — preauthorized transfers
title: Written authorization for recurring debits from a consumer bank/debit account, with a copy to the consumer
summary: Preauthorized (recurring) electronic fund transfers from a consumer's account — e.g. a subscription billed to a debit card, prepaid card or bank account (ACH) — may be authorized only by a writing signed or similarly authenticated by the consumer, and the merchant that obtains the authorization must give the consumer a copy of it.
remedies: EFTA § 1693m: actual damages plus statutory damages of $100-$1,000 per individual (class: lesser of $500,000 or 1% of net worth, unverified) and attorney's fees. Critical when debit or ACH billing is confirmed; the copy of the authorization should reach the consumer before the first debit (CFPB guidance).

law: Electronic Fund Transfer Act / Regulation E — preauthorized transfers
title: Advance notice when a recurring debit will change in amount
summary: When a preauthorized debit from a consumer's account will vary in amount from the previous transfer or from the authorized amount (e.g. a subscription price increase billed to a debit card or by ACH), the payee must send written notice of the amount and date of the transfer at least 10 days before the scheduled transfer date.
notice_window: at least 10 days before the charge
remedies: EFTA § 1693m: actual damages plus statutory damages of $100-$1,000 per individual (class cap unverified) and attorney's fees.

law: California Automatic Renewal Law
title: Present the automatic-renewal offer terms clearly and conspicuously, next to the consent request
summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal offer terms (§ 17601(a)(2)): that the subscription continues until the consumer cancels; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and, if the amount may change, that it may change and the new amount if known); the length of the renewal term or that the service is continuous; and any minimum purchase obligation — clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity (for voice offers, temporal proximity) to the request for consent to the offer.
remedies: No private right in the ARL itself (Mayron v. Google, 2020): plaintiffs sue under the UCL, FAL and CLRA and must show economic injury; CLRA requires a 30-day demand letter before damages. Goods or services provided without the required consent are an unconditional gift (§ 17603); all civil remedies are available (§ 17604, with a good-faith-compliance safe harbor). Public enforcement by the district attorneys' task force (CART): penalties plus restitution (HelloFresh $7.5M). Typical class settlements $0.6M-$7.5M.

summary: A business that lets consumers accept an offer online must let them terminate exclusively online, at will, and without further steps that obstruct or delay immediate termination, via either a prominently located direct link or button (in the account/profile or device/user settings) or an immediately accessible termination email formatted and provided by the business that the consumer can send without additional information. Private plaintiffs plead GBL § 349; no authority found on whether a § 527-a breach alone suffices. Goods sent without affirmative consent are an unconditional gift (§ 527-a(2)).

law: New York Automatic Renewal Law (Prohibited Service Offer Practices)
title: Notice of material changes before implementation (2021-2025 text)
summary: Before implementing a material change to accepted terms, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
citation: former N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 527-a(4), (5)(b) (L. 2020, ch. 267)
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Attorney General enforcement: civil penalties of $100-$1,000 per violation (secondary figure) and restitution (1-800-Flowers $375K plus nationwide restitution; Equinox $600K). Private plaintiffs plead GBL § 349; no authority found on whether a § 527-a breach alone suffices. Goods sent without affirmative consent are an unconditional gift (§ 527-a(2)).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: disclose the material terms before consent or billing information, next to the consent request
summary: Before requesting consent or billing information, clearly and conspicuously disclose the material terms — the product, the amount and frequency of charges, the deadline (by date or frequency) by which the consumer must act to stop further charges, how to cancel, and any trial or temporary-price terms — in visual proximity to the request for consent.
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: cancellation as easy to use as the consent mechanism, in the same medium
summary: Provide a cancellation mechanism that is as easy to use as the mechanism the consumer used to consent and that is available through the same medium (an online sign-up must be cancellable online).
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: offer online cancellation (website or email) for in-person sign-ups
summary: Allow cancellation through every medium in which consent can be given. Where consent was obtained in person, also offer an online cancellation mechanism (website or email) — a telephone line alone is not enough (state law allows online or phone).
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: do not obstruct, ignore or unreasonably delay cancellation (save offers included)
summary: Do not obscure cancellation instructions, hang up on consumers, refuse to acknowledge a cancellation request or unreasonably delay processing it; save (retention) offers are allowed only if they do not impose unreasonable conditions on, or unreasonably delay, the cancellation (§ 5-110.1(e)(2)).
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: renewal notice 15-45 days before the cancellation deadline for one-year-plus terms
summary: Where the initial paid term is one year or longer and the plan renews for a paid term of six months or longer, notify the consumer 15 to 45 days before the cancellation deadline, in the manner the consumer selected (text, email, app notification or another channel offered), with instructions on how to cancel.
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: notice of material changes, including price increases, 5 business days to 30 days in advance
summary: Give the consumer a clear and conspicuous notice of any material change to the terms, including a price increase, at least five business days and no more than thirty days before the change, in the manner the consumer selected.
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: notice 3-21 days before a free trial of more than a month converts to paid
summary: If a free gift or trial lasts more than a month and is followed by an automatic charge, notify the consumer 3 to 21 days before the cancellation deadline for the first chargeable period, in the manner the consumer selected, with instructions on how to cancel.
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
title: NYC: refund everything charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel
summary: A business that violates the rule must refund every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt at cancellation. Honour the first cancellation attempt (confirm it and stop charging) so no charge follows it.
remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

law: Alaska free trial period law
title: Clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms of a free trial
summary: When offering, promoting or advertising goods or services for a free trial period, clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms: restrictions, limitations and conditions (including any minimum purchase obligation after the trial), a description of all charges imposed after the trial (including shipping and handling), the consumer's right to cancel, and any other obligations assumed by accepting the trial.
remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Alaska free trial period law
title: Obtain express verifiable consent to the free trial
summary: Before providing goods or services for a free trial period, obtain the consumer's express verifiable consent to the free trial.
remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Alaska free trial period law
title: Allow cancellation during the trial and a refund within 30 days after it ends
summary: A consumer may return the goods or cancel the services at any time during the free trial without further obligation, and within 30 days after the trial ends may return the goods or cancel for a full refund of charges (or a partial refund for the unused portion).
remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request; explain post-trial pricing
summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the offer terms (§ 4-86-112(a)(8)): that the subscription continues until cancelled; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and any change in amount); the length of the term unless chosen by the consumer; and any minimum purchase obligation, clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity (or, for verbal offers, temporal proximity) to the request for consent. If the offer includes a free gift or trial, clearly and conspicuously explain the price charged after the trial or how pricing will change.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Obtain consent before charging and express consent to the offer terms
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account without first obtaining consent to the agreement containing the offer terms (including promotional or discounted terms), and obtain the consumer's express consent to the offer terms.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Do not undermine consent or misrepresent material facts
summary: Do not include contract information that interferes with, detracts from, contradicts or undermines the consumer's consent, and do not misrepresent any material fact, including that the plan automatically renews or facts about the underlying goods or services.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Keep verification of consent for three years (or one year after termination, if longer)
summary: Maintain verification of the consumer's consent for at least three years, or one year after the contract is terminated, whichever is longer.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for trials explain how to cancel before paying
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, the cancellation policy and how to cancel (describing the cancellation mechanism). If the offer includes a free gift or trial, disclose how to cancel it and allow cancellation before the consumer pays.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Notice before a free trial or promotional price longer than 31 days ends
summary: If the consumer accepted a free gift or trial (or promotional price) lasting more than 31 days, send the § 4-86-112(b)(8) notice — renewal statement, renewal length and terms, amount/range and frequency of charges, cancellation methods, a cancellation link if sent electronically, contact information — 3 to 21 days before the period expires.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Renewal notice for initial terms of one year or longer
summary: For an initial term of one year or longer, send the § 4-86-112(b)(8) notice 15 to 45 days before the subscription renews.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Cancellation mechanism; phone lines answered promptly; voicemail handled within one business day
summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment. If a toll-free number is offered, answer calls promptly during business hours without obstruction, and process a voicemail cancellation request (or call back) within one business day.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel online, at will, immediately
summary: If the consumer accepted online, allow termination exclusively online, at will and without steps that obstruct or delay immediate termination, through a prominently located direct link or button (account/profile or device/user settings) or an immediately accessible pre-formatted termination email. Account authentication may be required, with an offline alternative for consumers who cannot authenticate online.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Save offers only with a continuously displayed "click to cancel" option
summary: Retention offers are allowed only if the consumer can still cancel: online, any offer must be shown with a prominently located, continuously and proximately displayed "click to cancel" link or button; by phone, the consumer must first be told they can cancel at any time by saying "cancel". Using that option must promptly cancel the subscription.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Cancellation in the same medium used to sign up
summary: Cancellation must be available in the medium used to activate the subscription or the medium the consumer usually uses with the business; for phone activations, a retainable cancellation phone number must be clearly and conspicuously displayed on the website.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Notice of material changes before they take effect
summary: Before implementing a material change, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Fee-change notice 7 to 30 days in advance
summary: For any change in the fee (including changes the consumer previously agreed to), give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable cancellation information no less than 7 and no more than 30 days before it takes effect.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
title: Annual reminder of the subscription terms
summary: Send an annual reminder to consumers under an annual automatic renewal or continuous service agreement, in the medium that activated it or the consumer's usual medium, disclosing the product or service, the frequency and amount of charges, and how to cancel.
remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Present the automatic renewal offer terms clearly and conspicuously before the contract is executed
summary: Before the contract is executed, clearly and conspicuously present the automatic renewal offer terms: that the contract will renew or extend after the initial period for a set term not exceeding one year (unless the consumer gives express written consent to a longer term); the cancellation policy; any recurring charges; the length of the renewal term; and any minimum purchase obligation. Voice offers: in temporal proximity to the consent request. Trial offers must also clearly and conspicuously explain the price and any further purchase obligations after the trial.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Links to renewal details must be adjacent to the purchase link and labelled as an auto-renewal enrollment
summary: An online link to detailed automatic-renewal information may be used only if it is available before the consumer elects to purchase, appears directly adjacent to the link used to purchase, and is labelled with (or directly adjacent to) a clear and conspicuous statement that by purchasing the consumer agrees to enroll in an automatic renewal contract.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Send a retainable written acknowledgment; for trials explain how to cancel before paying
summary: Provide a written acknowledgment, retainable by the consumer, with the automatic renewal offer terms, the cancellation policy and how to cancel. For trial offers, explain how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer must pay.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: One-step online cancellation link
summary: Provide a simple, cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use and readily accessible cancellation mechanism. Safe harbor: for consumers who consented online or through an electronic communication, a one-step online cancellation link — on the website, in the device or service, or in an electronic communication — available immediately after a reasonable authentication used solely to confirm authority over the account; for other consents, a one-step online link or a qualifying in-person mechanism where the consumer regularly uses the goods or services. "One-step online cancellation" means no additional action that obstructs or delays immediate termination.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Online save offers only with a continuously displayed direct cancel link
summary: When a consumer cancels online, a discounted offer, retention benefit or information about the effects of cancelling may be shown only if a prominently located, continuously proximate direct link to cancel is displayed alongside it; if the consumer uses that link the cancellation must be processed promptly without further obstruction or delay.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
summary: If a material change occurs in an accepted automatic renewal contract, provide a retainable, clear and conspicuous notice of the change and information on cancelling, including the cancellation mechanism.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
title: Renewal notice 25-40 days before renewal (yearly for terms under 12 months)
summary: Notify the consumer by mail, email, or (if authorized or customary) text or app message that the contract will automatically renew unless cancelled, with the cancellation process and the sender's identity, 25 to 40 days before the first automatic renewal and each later renewal. For renewal terms shorter than 12 months, send it at least once in the 25-40 days before the renewal that would extend the contract beyond each continuous 12-month period.
remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Disclose the renewal / continuous-service terms clearly and conspicuously
summary: Disclose clearly and conspicuously (retainably, if electronic or written): that the business will automatically renew or continue the service until the consumer acts; the actions needed to stop it (with a link or other electronic means if disclosed electronically); all recurring charges and any known change in amount; the renewal term length or service duration; other renewal provisions; any minimum purchase obligation; and the business's contact information. Continuous-service terms must be disclosed before the consumer enters the agreement; automatic-renewal terms "before such automatic renewal".
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Disclose the post-trial price before the consumer enters the agreement
summary: If the agreement includes a free gift or trial period, clearly and conspicuously disclose, before the consumer enters the agreement, the price charged after the period and any way pricing will change after it.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging; keep a lawful record of it
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party payment account for any renewal or continuous service (including at a promotional or discounted price) without the consumer's affirmative consent. Since Oct. 1, 2025, agencies and courts consider whether the business produced a record of consent obtained lawfully (including under the telephone recording laws).
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Notice during free trials or promotional periods of 32 days or more
summary: For agreements offered electronically or by phone with a free gift, trial, or discounted/promotional price period, disclose electronically or by phone: that the agreement will renew or continue until the consumer acts; the renewal term or service duration; other renewal provisions; how to stop it; and (if offered electronically) the direct cancellation link/button or email. Timing: for periods of at least 32 days, at least 21 days after the period starts and "not earlier than three days before" it expires; for periods of at least one year, 15 to 45 days before it expires.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Notice 15-45 days before a free trial or promotional period of one year or more ends
summary: For agreements offered electronically or by phone with a free gift, trial, or discounted/promotional price period of at least one year, give the § 42-158ff(b)(1)(F) notice (renewal or continuation until the consumer acts, the renewal term, other renewal provisions, how to stop it, and the direct cancellation link/button or email) 15 to 45 days before the period expires.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Disclose material changes before making them
summary: Before making a material change to the automatic renewal or continuous service terms, clearly and conspicuously disclose the change and the actions the consumer must take to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Maintain a channel consumers can use to stop renewal
summary: Establish and maintain an email address, postal address, or the telephone number or online means required by § 42-158ff(e) that consumers can use to prevent renewal or terminate continuous service.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Online agreements must be cancellable online without any offline step or obstruction
summary: A business that enters into an agreement online must let the consumer take every action needed to stop renewal or terminate the service online, without requiring offline action, and may not obstruct or delay those efforts. Account authentication may be required, but a consumer unable or unwilling to authenticate online must be able to cancel offline.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Cancel by prominent link/button, reply email, or a retainable phone number shown on the website
summary: Every business with an automatic renewal or continuous services agreement must let consumers cancel by a prominently displayed direct link or button (in the account/profile or device/user settings), an immediately accessible email the consumer can reply to without more information, or a retainable telephone number clearly and conspicuously displayed on the business's website.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: No obstruction; phone line and voicemail rules; phone save offers only after the "say cancel" disclosure
summary: Do not obstruct or delay cancellation. A cancellation phone line must be answered promptly during normal business hours; a cancellation voicemail must be processed (or the call returned) within one business day, and processed within one business day if the consumer cannot be reached and the voicemail has enough information. On calls, retention offers may be made only after clearly telling the consumer they can cancel at any time by saying "cancel".
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
title: Annual reminder for every automatic renewal or continuous services agreement
summary: From July 1, 2026, send each consumer an annual reminder identifying the goods or services, how to stop renewal or terminate, and the frequency and amount of the charges — in the manner the subscription was activated (if not in person) or the consumer's usual channel, otherwise by email, mail or phone.
remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
title: Disclose the automatic renewal provision and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
summary: A contract that automatically renews at the end of a definite term must disclose the automatic renewal provision and the cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously in the contract, visually proximate to any request for consent.
remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
title: Explain the post-trial price
summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial, clearly and conspicuously explain the price charged after the trial ends or how the subscription price will change when it ends.
remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ initial terms), every year
summary: For an initial term of 12 months or more that renews for one month or more, notify the consumer of the first renewal and annually thereafter, 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, by first-class mail, email, or another accessible form the consumer authorized, disclosing clearly and conspicuously: that it will renew unless cancelled; the cost for the renewal term; the cancellation deadline; and how to get details of the renewal and cancellation procedures. Email notices must include active links to cancel.
remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
title: Trial notice 15-30 days before a free trial of one month or more ends
summary: For a free trial with a term of one month or more that automatically renews when the trial ends, notify the consumer of the automatic renewal 15 to 30 days before the trial expires.
remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
title: Separate affirmative consent to the automatic renewal after a free trial
summary: Notwithstanding the consumer's consent to the free trial, obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the automatic renewal before charging for it.
remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
title: Disclose the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously when the contract is made
summary: A seller whose consumer contract contains an automatic renewal provision must disclose the terms of that provision clearly and conspicuously at the time the contract is entered into.
remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
title: Notice of each extension 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline
summary: For a contract renewed for more than one month at a time where the renewal keeps it in effect more than 12 months after it began, notify the consumer of each upcoming extension 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously: that it will renew unless cancelled; the date by which to cancel; the procedure to cancel (an online procedure if the consumer contracted online); and how to obtain the renewal provision details.
remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
title: Easy cancellation for any auto-renewing contract; online sign-ups cancel online
summary: For any contract that automatically renews — regardless of the renewal period — failing to provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism is a deceptive practice; a consumer who contracted online must be allowed to cancel online.
remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
title: Disclose the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in the contract or offer
summary: A seller of a service contract with an automatic renewal provision must disclose the provision clearly and conspicuously in the contract or contract offer.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ service contracts
summary: For a service contract with a term of 12 months or more that renews for more than one month, give written or electronic notice of the automatic renewal provision 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that the contract will renew unless cancelled and how to obtain details of the renewal provision and the cancellation procedure.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
title: Allow cancellation in the same manner and by the same means as acceptance
summary: A seller that enters into or renews a service contract with an automatic renewal provision must allow the consumer to cancel in the same manner, and by the same means, as the consumer accepted the contract.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the offer terms — the cancellation policy, the recurring charges (and any known change in amount), the length of the renewal term or that the service is continuous, and any minimum purchase obligation — clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity to the request for consent.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Obtain consent before charging
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party payment account without first obtaining the consumer's consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Send an easily retained acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel
summary: Provide an acknowledgment of the offer terms (on the business's website, via a link to platform-specific instructions, or otherwise in a manner easily retained), including the cancellation policy and how to cancel and a description of the cancellation mechanism (toll-free number, email, postal address if billing directly, or another cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use mechanism). It may follow the initial order.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Charge notice before or within three days after charging
summary: Unless the consumer opted out, send a notice before charging the consumer or within three days after the charge, stating clearly and conspicuously: that the subscription will automatically renew unless cancelled; the length and other terms of the renewal period; a link or other electronic way to reach the cancellation process (if sent electronically); and the business's contact information.
notice_window: before the charge or up to 3 days after it
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel online; describe the cancellation mechanism
summary: A business that lets consumers accept online must let them cancel online, e.g. via a clear and conspicuous link to a website or online cancellation service or a pre-formatted cancellation email; it may require account authentication, with an offline alternative for consumers who cannot authenticate online. It must also provide a toll-free number, email, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
summary: For a material change in an accepted online offer, provide a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and easily retained information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
summary: For a consumer contract with a term of more than one month that automatically renews for more than one month, disclose the automatic renewal clause and the cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously in the contract.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Disclose the continuous service clause and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
summary: For a consumer contract with a continuous service clause (continues until cancelled), clearly and conspicuously disclose the clause and the cancellation procedure.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account for an automatic renewal or continuous service without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for trials state the right to cancel before paying
summary: Provide an acknowledgment the consumer may retain with the offer terms, cancellation policy and cancellation procedure. For free trials it must also clearly and conspicuously state the right to cancel before payment and how.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ contracts)
summary: For a contract term of 12 months or more that renews for more than one month, notify the consumer clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled, how to cancel, and the deadline to respond, 30 to 60 days before that deadline. Electronic notice is allowed if the sale was electronic (UETA) or the consumer elected email notices.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Provide a cancellation channel and honor cancellation requests
summary: Include a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or a clearly and conspicuously described cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use alternative to communicate cancellation; knowingly failing to cancel upon the consumer's request is an unfair or deceptive practice.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
title: Notice of material changes before implementation
summary: Before implementing a material change, clearly and conspicuously notify Hawaii consumers of the change with retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
title: Clearly and conspicuously disclose the renewal terms and the ways to cancel
summary: An online automatic subscription renewal offer must clearly and conspicuously disclose the automatic renewal terms and the methods the consumer may use to cancel.
remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
title: Offer a free, easy online cancellation mechanism; phone numbers must be toll-free and prominent
summary: Provide cancellation methods that include a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use online mechanism (which may be a pre-formatted termination email), without an additional cancellation fee; any cancellation phone number must be toll-free and prominently displayed in the disclosure.
remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days ahead for subscriptions renewing for 12 months or more
summary: For an extended automatic subscription renewal (renewing for a term of 12 months or more), notify the consumer 30 to 60 days before the goods or services are delivered or provided, clearly and conspicuously describing them, stating the price, saying they will be provided unless the consumer declines, and giving one or more cancellation methods (including at least one at no cost), with the same online cancellation methods as § 48-603G(3).
remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Disclose the automatic renewal offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
summary: Disclose clearly and conspicuously in the contract, before the subscription is fulfilled and in visual proximity (for voice offers, temporal proximity) to the consent request, the automatic renewal offer terms: that the subscription continues until cancelled; the timeframe in which the consumer must cancel to avoid the next charge; the recurring charges (and any change); the renewal term length or that service is continuous; and any minimum purchase obligation.
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause, including the cancellation procedure (2005-2023 text)
summary: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously in the contract, including the cancellation procedure.
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Obtain consent before charging
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or other payment mechanism for an automatic renewal without first obtaining the consumer's consent to the contract containing the automatic renewal offer terms.
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; explain how to cancel a free trial before paying
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the automatic renewal offer terms, the cancellation policy and how to cancel (a link to platform-specific instructions is acceptable). If the offer includes a free gift or trial, disclose how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer pays.
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Notice during a free trial or promotional period of 15 days or more
summary: If the contract includes a free trial or promotional period lasting 15 days or longer, notify the consumer during that period, at least 3 days before the cancellation deadline in the automatic renewal offer terms, using a method the consumer is accustomed to using with the business.
notice_window: at least 3 days before the cancellation deadline
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ contracts)
summary: For a contract with a term of 12 months or more that renews for more than one month, give written notice 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously and in retainable form: that it will renew unless cancelled; a cancellation mechanism offered in a manner the consumer commonly uses with the business; and the deadline to cancel to avoid the next charge.
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
title: Online offers: cancellation mechanism, and online sign-ups can cancel exclusively online
summary: A business making automatic renewal or continuous service offers online must provide a toll-free number, email, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism; a consumer who accepted online must be allowed to terminate exclusively online (e.g. a pre-formatted termination email or a link to a website or online service for cancelling).
remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request; explain post-trial pricing
summary: Before the agreement is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal or continuous service offer terms (continues until cancelled; cancellation policy; recurring charges and any change; term length or continuous service; minimum purchase obligation) clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or, for voice, temporal) proximity to the consent request. Free gifts or trials must include a clear and conspicuous explanation of the post-trial price.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
summary: Obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the agreement with the offer terms (including promotional or discounted terms) before charging the consumer's card or third-party account.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment describing how to cancel; trials cancellable before payment
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel, describing the cancellation mechanism; for free gifts or trials, explain how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer pays.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel exclusively online
summary: A consumer who accepted online must be allowed to terminate exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the business that can be sent without additional information.
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
summary: For a material change in accepted terms, provide a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

law: Louisiana contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously
summary: A seller under a contract that automatically renews unless the consumer cancels must disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously in the contract or contract offer.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel
summary: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel the contract in the initial contract, the contract offer, or with delivery of the products or services.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the acceptance request; explain post-trial pricing
summary: Before the agreement is fulfilled, present clearly and conspicuously, in visual proximity to the request for acceptance (temporal proximity for voice offers), the offer terms: that the contract renews for a set term not exceeding one year unless the consumer gives express written consent to a longer term; the cancellation policy; any recurring charges; the renewal term length; and any minimum purchase obligation. Free or discounted trials must explain the price after the trial or how pricing will change.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Obtain affirmative consent; do not undermine express acceptance
summary: Do not charge the consumer's payment method without first obtaining affirmative consent to an agreement that clearly and conspicuously displays the renewal terms (including promotional-price terms), and do not include information that contradicts or undermines the consumer's express affirmative acceptance.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Keep records of consent for at least one year
summary: Maintain reasonable business records sufficient to demonstrate the consumer's affirmative consent for at least one year from contract formation.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Notice before confirming billing information
summary: Before confirming the consumer's billing information, give a clear and conspicuous notice stating that the service will automatically renew unless cancelled, the length and other terms of the renewal period, the amount or range of costs and the frequency of charges, one or more ways to cancel, and the business's contact information.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for trials or discounts explain how to cancel before being charged
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and cancellation instructions; for discounts, free gifts or trial periods, explain how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer is charged.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation that is not designed to deter
summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism to cancel the contract or trial, avoid charges or increased charges, and stop future charges, that is not unreasonably burdensome or designed to deter cancellation, available online or by email, telephone or another commonly used method.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Notice of material changes, including price increases, before the renewal at which they apply
summary: Give a clear and conspicuous, retainable notice of any material change, with information on how to cancel (including the simple mechanism); for material changes including price increases, the pre-renewal notice (renewal terms, amount to be charged, cancellation instructions) must be given at least 3 days before the renewal.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Pre-renewal notice for renewal terms of twelve months or longer
summary: If the renewal term is twelve months or longer, give notice at least 3 days before the renewal with the renewal terms, the amount to be charged and how to cancel.
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
title: Notice before a trial converts to a paid subscription
summary: When a contract converts from a trial period to a paid subscription, give notice at least 3 days before the conversion with the renewal terms, the amount to be charged and how to cancel.
notice_window: at least 3 days before the trial ends
remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Trial offers: written disclosure of obligations and the calendar cancel-by and charge dates
summary: Before the consumer accepts a trial offer, disclose clearly, conspicuously and in writing: any financial obligations that may result; all products for which the consumer may incur an obligation; how to reject or cancel before incurring an obligation; the calendar date by which the consumer must cancel; and the calendar date on which the obligation begins if the consumer does not cancel.
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Negative-option products: written disclosure of the charge, its recurrence, and how to cancel
summary: Before purchase of a product with a negative option feature, disclose clearly, conspicuously and in writing: that the consumer will be charged (or that charges will increase after any trial); if applicable, that charges recur until the consumer takes steps to stop them; and how to cancel using the simple mechanism required by 940 CMR 38.05(3).
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Simple cancellation as easy as sign-up, through the same website/app, that immediately stops charges
summary: Provide a simple mechanism to cancel the negative option feature, avoid being charged and immediately stop recurring charges, at least as easy to access and use as the method used to sign up and available through the same medium: internet sign-ups through the same website or app; telephone through a number answered promptly during business hours and no more costly than the sign-up call; in-person sales through the internet or a telephone number plus, where practical, an in-person method.
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Pre-deadline notice 5-30 days ahead for negative option periods over 31 days
summary: For a negative option feature exceeding 31 days, send written notice 5 to 30 calendar days before the date by which the consumer must cancel to avoid the next obligation, disclosing clearly and conspicuously: the obligations; the products; the cancellation mechanism; the cancel-by calendar date; and the charge date — through a medium similar to the one used to sign up or a common medium the consumer affirmatively chose.
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Pre-deadline notice 5-30 days before a trial longer than 31 days converts
summary: Where the period before the negative option charge (e.g. a free trial) exceeds 31 days, send the 940 CMR 38.05(4) written notice 5 to 30 calendar days before the cancel-by date.
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
title: Plans of 31 days or less: pre-deadline notice or a per-charge notice with cancel instructions
summary: For negative option contracts of 31 days or less (e.g. monthly plans), either send the 940 CMR 38.05(4) notice, or, at least as often as the consumer is charged, a written notice disclosing clearly and conspicuously the amount charged at renewal and how to cancel to avoid further charges, through a similar or commonly used medium.
notice_window: up to 30 days before the charge or up to 3 days after it
remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal offer terms — including the price charged after the initial term ends or how the agreement will change at the end of it — clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity to the request for consent (for oral offers, at the same time as the request).
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Disclose the cancellation methods in an easily accessible way
summary: Present the consumer with an easily accessible disclosure of the methods the consumer may use to cancel the automatic renewal.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Explain the post-trial price
summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial, clearly and conspicuously explain the price charged after the trial and how pricing will change at its end.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Notice and consent before automatically charging a credit card (initial terms over one month)
summary: For an automatic renewal offer with an initial definite term of more than one month, do not automatically charge the consumer's credit card unless clear and conspicuous notice is given and the consumer consents to the automatic charge.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Cancellation as easy as sign-up, same medium, prominent link/button or email, no required live agent
summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism to cancel, avoid (increased) charges and immediately stop recurring charges, without unreasonable delay, hindrance or obstruction. It must be at least as easy as the consent mechanism and available in the same medium. Online cancellation must be easy to find, must not require talking to a live or virtual representative (unless sign-up did), and must include a prominently placed direct link or button (in the account/profile or device/user settings) or an immediately accessible pre-formatted termination email. Phone cancellation must be performed promptly on a number that is answered or records messages during business hours; in-person cancellation must resemble the in-person sign-up and also offer the online and phone options.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Notice 3-21 days before a free gift or trial longer than 14 days converts
summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial lasting more than 14 days, give a clear and conspicuous notice 3 to 21 days before the automatic renewal takes effect, stating: that it will renew unless cancelled; the duration and terms of the renewal (including the post-trial price); the ways to cancel; a cancellation link if sent electronically; and contact information.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
title: Renewal notice 15-45 days ahead for initial terms of at least one year
summary: If the consumer accepted an initial term of at least one year, give the § 14-1329(c)(1) notice 15 to 45 days before the automatic renewal takes effect.
remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Clear, conspicuous and easily accessible disclosure of all material terms and the ways to cancel
summary: Present a clear, conspicuous and easily accessible disclosure of all material terms of the renewal offer — including the amount and frequency of charges and the refund policy on cancellation — and of the methods the consumer may use to cancel; any cancellation phone number must be toll-free and prominently displayed in the disclosure. No misrepresentation of material facts about the renewal offer.
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Express consent to the renewal by check box, e-signature or other affirmative action
summary: Before enrollment, obtain the consumer's express consent to the automatic renewal through a check box, electronic signature or other affirmative action agreeing to the renewal offer.
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Cancellation by the same method and in the same manner as sign-up
summary: Provide for cancellation of the subscription or membership using the same method, and in the same manner, by which the consumer initially agreed to it (an online sign-up must be cancellable online).
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Renewal notice no more than 30 days before renewal for 12-month+ subscriptions
summary: For an extended renewal (subscription term of 12 months or more renewing for more than one month), notify the consumer no more than 30 days before the renewal date, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled and where to obtain details of the renewal and cancellation procedure.
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Disclose the ways to cancel and provide online cancellation (2020-2025 text)
