remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ subscriptions (2020-2025 text)
summary: For an extended automatic subscription renewal (term of 12 months or more renewing for more than one month), notify the consumer 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled and where to obtain details of the renewal and cancellation procedure; online cancellation required.
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Maine charges after free trial period
title: Free offers: get billing information directly from the consumer and disclose the free-offer terms
summary: A seller may not make a free offer (one that obligates the consumer to pay unless they contact the seller) unless, when the consumer agrees, the seller obtains the billing information directly from the consumer and clearly and conspicuously discloses the terms of the free offer, including any additional financial obligations.
remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously before acceptance, next to the offer
summary: Before the consumer accepts, present the offer terms (§ 325G.56, subd. 7): that the agreement continues until the consumer terminates it; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and any change); the renewal term or that service is continuous (unless chosen by the consumer); and any minimum purchase obligation, clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or, for voice offers, temporal) proximity to the offer.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: No charges before the agreement is authorized; consent required
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account before the agreement has been duly authorized by the seller and consumer and made effective; goods sent without the consumer's affirmative consent are an unconditional gift.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Timely retainable confirmation with the terms, trial cancellation and termination options
summary: In a timely manner after acceptance, send a retainable confirmation (email suffices) with the offer terms; for free trials, how to cancel before paying; and easy, cost-effective, timely termination options, including the website termination election for online sellers and, for sign-ups by other means, an option as easy and accessible as the original means of acceptance.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Notice of material changes before implementation (otherwise the change is void)
summary: Before implementing a material change, give a timely, clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to terminate; a material change made without it is void and unenforceable.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Notice 5-30 days before a free trial longer than 30 days ends
summary: If the offer includes a free trial lasting more than 30 days, notify the consumer 5 to 30 days before the trial ends of the option to cancel before the trial ends to avoid paying.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Yearly written notice for continuous-service subscriptions
summary: For a continuous-service agreement, give the consumer written notice of the continuous service by mail or email at least once per calendar year, including the terms of the service and how to terminate or manage it.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: No retention offers after a cancellation request unless the consumer opts in; no abusive tactics
summary: After receiving a cancellation or termination notice, the seller may not misrepresent or use unfair or abusive tactics to delay or avoid cancellation, and may not make retention offers, benefits, modifications or gifts unless the consumer grants permission after giving notice (asked only once per attempt). The seller may ask (without requiring an answer) why the consumer is cancelling, explain consequences, verify identity, and describe downgrade, pause or suspension options.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Website "termination election" for sellers with account or subscription management
summary: A seller whose website has profile or subscription-management capabilities must include a clear and conspicuous termination election that tells consumers in plain language they can terminate at any time, asks only for information needed to process the termination, and uses a checkbox, submit button or similarly simple mechanism — regardless of how the consumer signed up.
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
title: Honor terminations: end of term for renewals; within 31 days for continuous service
summary: A consumer may terminate at any time using the procedure in the confirmation. Automatic-renewal terminations take effect at the end of the current term (or a later term the consumer picks); continuous-service terminations must take effect no later than 31 days after a verified notice (unless the consumer chooses a later date).
remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously
summary: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously in the contract or contract offer.
remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel
summary: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel the contract in the initial contract, the contract offer, or with delivery of the products or services.
remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Written renewal notice 15-45 days before renewals longer than 60 days
summary: For any automatic renewal exceeding 60 days, give written notice by personal delivery, email or first-class mail 15 to 45 days before the renewal date, stating the date the contract will renew and that it will renew unless cancelled before then.
remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
title: Changed terms at renewal must be disclosed in the renewal notice in 12-point bold type
summary: If the contract terms will change upon automatic renewal, disclose the changing terms clearly and conspicuously in the renewal notification, in at least 12-point type and in bold print.
remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Present the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously, near the offer
summary: Present the terms of the automatic renewal offer clearly and conspicuously before the subscription or purchase agreement is fulfilled and in proximity to the offer.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: No charge without compliant disclosures and affirmative consent
summary: Do not charge the buyer's card, bank account or other financial account unless the § 51-37-02(1) requirements are met and the buyer gave affirmative consent to the agreement containing the automatic renewal terms.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Renewal periods may not exceed twelve months
summary: The renewal period in an automatic renewal provision may not exceed twelve months.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Retainable acknowledgment with the terms and a simple cancellation procedure
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the automatic renewal terms and how to cancel, describing a cost-effective, timely and simple cancellation procedure.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Provide a cost-effective, timely and simple cancellation procedure
summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely and simple procedure for cancellation, described in the acknowledgment.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days ahead for renewal periods over six months
summary: If the agreement renews for a period of more than six months, give clear and conspicuous written notice (first-class mail, email, or text/app if the consumer authorized it) that the buyer may cancel and avoid renewal, with the cancellation procedure, 30 to 60 days before the renewal date or the end of the cancellation period.
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
summary: If the terms materially change, give clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
title: Set out the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type
summary: A consumer service contract may contain an automatic renewal provision only if it is set forth clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type and states the notice requirements, the specific procedure to cancel at the end of the initial term, and the renewal terms that apply if no cancellation notice is given.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline, by certified mail or on a monthly statement
summary: Before the end of the initial term and of each renewal term, serve written notice specifying the cancellation procedure, clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type, by certified mail or on the first page of a monthly statement, 30 to 60 days before the last day on which the consumer may give notice of termination.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
title: Honor timely cancellation notices sent by any reliable means; no termination cost
summary: Allow at least 30 calendar days after the consumer receives the renewal notice to give notice of termination; honor cancellation notices sent by fax, mail, email or other reliable means (including timely-sent notices received late); and allow termination at the end of the initial or any renewal term without additional cost or penalty.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the offer terms (ORS 646A.293(5)): that the subscription continues until the consumer cancels; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and the new amount if it will change, if known); the renewal term length or that service is continuous; and any minimum purchase obligation, clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or, for voice offers, temporal) proximity to the request for consent.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party payment account without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms; goods sent without it are an unconditional gift.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; free trials cancellable before payment
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms and how to cancel (it may follow the initial order). For free trials, the acknowledgment must explain how to cancel, and the consumer must be allowed to cancel before paying.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, post-office address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
title: Notice of material changes before implementation
summary: Before implementing a material change, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon free offer law
title: Free offers: clear and conspicuous terms in close proximity to the consent request
summary: Before the consumer accepts a free offer that leads to a financial obligation, provide clear and conspicuous information, in close proximity to the consent request: all goods, services or enrollments the consumer will be obligated for; the cost; any need to take affirmative action to reject and how; that the consumer will be obligated unless they cancel; the right to cancel by toll-free call or in a manner substantially similar to acceptance; the time by which to cancel; and any return-credit rights.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon free offer law
title: Free offers: billing information directly from the consumer and affirmative consent
summary: Obtain billing information directly from the consumer (or with affirmative consent to its transfer) and obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the free-offer terms before imposing any financial obligation.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Oregon free offer law
title: Free offers: honor cancellation via the disclosed toll-free or same-manner procedure
summary: Do not fail or refuse to cancel a free offer when the consumer uses (or reasonably tries to use) the cancellation procedure — a toll-free number or a method substantially similar to how the consumer accepted.
remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: South Carolina automatic renewal provisions in service contracts
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline, with the renewal amount and how to cancel
summary: An automatic renewal provision in a service contract is unenforceable unless the consumer received written or electronic notice 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, conspicuously disclosing: that the contract will renew unless cancelled; the amount charged on renewal; and how to get details of the renewal and cancellation procedure, including a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism.
remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request; explain post-trial pricing
summary: Before the agreement is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal or continuous service offer terms (continues until cancelled; cancellation policy; recurring charges and any change; term length or continuous; minimum purchase obligation) clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or temporal) proximity to the consent request; for free gifts or trials, clearly and conspicuously explain the post-trial price.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Obtain affirmative consent (a clear, specific, informed, unambiguous act) before charging
summary: Before charging the consumer's card or third-party account, obtain affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms (including promotional-price terms) — "a clear, affirmative act signifying a consumer's freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous agreement", such as a written (including electronic) statement or an unambiguous affirmative action. A charge made without it must be refunded if the consumer asks within seven days of the charge.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Charge-date notice when a trial ends more than 60 days after sign-up
summary: If the automatic renewal will occur more than 60 days after affirmative consent (e.g. a long free trial), the entity billing the consumer must give a clear and conspicuous notice of when the consumer will be charged.
notice_window: any time before the trial ends
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Charge-date notice when the first renewal is more than 60 days after sign-up
summary: If the first automatic renewal will occur more than 60 days after affirmative consent (terms of about two months or longer), the entity billing the consumer must give a clear and conspicuous notice of when the consumer will be charged for the renewal.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment describing how to cancel; trials cancellable before payment
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel, describing the cancellation mechanism; for free gifts or trials, disclose how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer pays.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel exclusively online
summary: A business that lets consumers accept online must allow termination exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the business that can be sent without additional information.
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
summary: For a material change in accepted terms, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days ahead when the next paid term is longer than 45 days
summary: For a contract that automatically renews at the end of a definite paid term for a subsequent paid term longer than 45 days, send a notice 30 to 60 days before the renewal that clearly and conspicuously discloses the renewal date, the total renewal cost, and the options for cancelling.
remedies: Non-compliant renewal provisions are void; Division of Consumer Protection administrative fines and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

law: Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act
title: Trial-ending notice at least 3 days before any trial period offer expires
summary: For a trial period offer (a period to sample a product or service without payment), send a notice at least 3 days before the trial expires that clearly and conspicuously discloses the expiration date, the price (and any further purchase obligations) after it, and the options for cancelling.
notice_window: at least 3 days before the trial ends
remedies: Non-compliant renewal provisions are void; Division of Consumer Protection administrative fines and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously before the consumer is obligated, next to the consent request
summary: Before the consumer becomes obligated and before the initial order is completed, present the automatic renewal offer terms — continues until cancelled; the cancellation policy including how to find the cancellation mechanism; recurring charges and any change; each deadline (by date or frequency) to stop charges; the renewal term or that service is continuous; any minimum purchase obligation — clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or temporal) proximity to the request for consent.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
summary: Before the initial order is completed, do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for free trials explain how to cancel before paying
summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel; if the offer includes a free trial, also disclose how to cancel the trial before the consumer pays or becomes obligated to pay.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Cancellation at least as easy as sign-up, through every sign-up channel, without a required agent
summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism that is clear and conspicuous and easy to find; at least as easy as the sign-up mechanism; available through each method by which consumers can sign up (in-person sign-ups: online or by phone); no required interaction with a live or virtual agent unless sign-up is only possible through one; phone cancellation effectuated promptly on a number answered or recording messages during business hours, free of charge and no more costly than sign-up; print publications sold in person, by pamphlet or mail must be cancellable online or by phone.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Cancellation mechanism described in the acknowledgment (2018-2026 text)
summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (only if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Conspicuous online cancellation option for online sellers (2022-2026 text)
summary: Each supplier making automatic renewal or continuous service offers through an online website must make available a conspicuous online option to cancel a recurring purchase.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Notice of material changes before implementation
summary: Before implementing a material change in accepted terms, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.
notice_window: any time before the price change
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Notice within the last 30 days of a free trial longer than 30 days
summary: For a free trial lasting more than 30 days, notify the consumer within 30 days of the end of the trial of the option to cancel before the trial ends to avoid an obligation to pay.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days ahead for renewals extending the contract by more than 12 months
summary: For an offer that renews after more than 30 days and extends the contract for more than 12 months, notify the consumer of the option to cancel 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline or the end of the current term, conspicuously disclosing that it will renew unless cancelled, the cancel-by date, how to cancel, and a copy of the renewal provisions.
remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
title: State the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously, in plain language and bold-face type
summary: The contract must state the terms of the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in plain, unambiguous language in bold-face type.
remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
title: Separate affirmative opt-in to the automatic renewal
summary: In addition to accepting the contract, the consumer must take an affirmative action to opt in to the automatic renewal provision.
remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the earliest of renewal, termination or cancellation deadline
summary: If the consumer opted in, send written or electronic notice 30 to 60 days before the earliest of the automatic renewal date, the termination date, or the date by which the consumer must give notice to cancel, stating the date the contract will terminate with a clear statement that it will renew automatically unless cancelled on or before that date, and the length and any additional terms of the renewal period.
remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
summary: Provide a toll-free telephone number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism for cancelling.
remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel exclusively online
summary: If the consumer accepted the contract online, permit termination exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the seller that the consumer can send without additional information.
remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
title: Terms must not deny the simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
summary: ROSCA requires simple mechanisms for consumers to stop recurring charges. Terms of service or policies that say a subscription cannot be canceled, or that it can only be canceled by phone, mail or in writing, contradict that mechanism and mislead subscribers about how to stop the charges.
remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
title: Refund and cancellation terms must match what the offer promises
summary: All material terms of a negative-option offer must be disclosed clearly before billing information is collected. A refund or money-back promise made in marketing or at checkout that the written refund policy takes back ("no refunds", a shorter window) is a misrepresented material term.
remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

law: California Automatic Renewal Law
title: Terms must allow online sign-ups to cancel online, at will and immediately
summary: Consumers who accepted an automatic renewal offer online must be able to terminate exclusively online, at will, and without steps that obstruct or delay immediate termination. Terms that require a phone call, a letter, written notice or a notice period before cancelling conflict with that right.
remedies: No private right in the ARL itself (Mayron v. Google, 2020): plaintiffs sue under the UCL, FAL and CLRA and must show economic injury; CLRA requires a 30-day demand letter before damages. Goods or services provided without the required consent are an unconditional gift (§ 17603); all civil remedies are available (§ 17604, with a good-faith-compliance safe harbor). Public enforcement by the district attorneys' task force (CART): penalties plus restitution (HelloFresh $7.5M). Typical class settlements $0.6M-$7.5M.

law: California Automatic Renewal Law
title: Terms of service restate the automatic renewal offer terms
summary: The automatic renewal offer terms (that the subscription continues until canceled, the cancellation policy, the recurring charges, the renewal term and how to cancel) must be presented clearly before the subscription is fulfilled. The Terms of service the consumer agrees to should state the same terms, so the contract does not silently differ from the checkout disclosure.
remedies: No private right in the ARL itself (Mayron v. Google, 2020): plaintiffs sue under the UCL, FAL and CLRA and must show economic injury; CLRA requires a 30-day demand letter before damages. Goods or services provided without the required consent are an unconditional gift (§ 17603); all civil remedies are available (§ 17604, with a good-faith-compliance safe harbor). Public enforcement by the district attorneys' task force (CART): penalties plus restitution (HelloFresh $7.5M). Typical class settlements $0.6M-$7.5M.
